ideas.title: The dowsing stone on a cord
ideas.goal: The player hangs the magnet stone from a grass cord in Lumi's beak and walks the beach; the stone swings towards hidden iron before you see it, spikes leap up off the sand and cling to it, and you learn to read the swing to find buried iron. Fun because the swing is a real pendulum you steer with your walk and the island tugs back.
ideas.toward: Step 1 of Sparks from stones made honest: the stone is HELD (beak_tips, s150) and every pull is the em.jl field, no scripted motion; the first time the player carries a field around
ideas.idea: A cord of 12 segments (position-based rope, length constraint) from Lumi's real beak tip to the stone; the stone is a rigid body with gravity, air drag and the em.jl force and torque from every spike and buried iron near it. Spikes are solved by softiron.jl, so they jump up and hang in chains under the swinging stone. Friends stop, stare, one gets a spike stuck to its pot. Someone watching sees the stone lean off the vertical towards nothing, then the sand below it bursts into leaping spikes.
ideas.form: plugins/magnetstone.jl: carrying becomes the cord; a 10 s traced film from the side, Lumi's whole body and the stone in frame, friends reacting

ideas.title: Two stones under one patch: where is it?
ideas.goal: A guessing game with the friends: two magnet stones are buried at random under a sand patch; the player sprinkles iron sand, taps, reads the lines, and plants a flag where each stone lies; the friends dig and cheer or groan. Fun because reading a real field gets learnable: two lobes for a lying stone, a tuft for a standing one, lines that bridge two stones.
ideas.toward: Iron sand project step 3 and the 'one field solver' promise: two sources superpose with no special case
ideas.idea: physics/ironsand.jl with two buried dipoles of random pose and depth; grains turn only where the field's torque beats friction, so depth reads as how far the pattern reaches. The friends' digging is real: they dig at the flag and the stone comes up (or doesn't).
ideas.form: plugin on the ironsand patch: a minigame with a score; a top-down traced film of the pattern forming and the dig

ideas.title: Strike a light: sparks from a stone
ideas.goal: The player strikes the iron spike down a flint from the cliff, harder or at a shallower angle, and a shower of real sparks flies; aim them into a tuft of dry grass and blow, and a fire catches, or doesn't. Fun because it is a skill: angle, speed, tinder and wind decide it.
ideas.toward: The big goal's title taken literally, and the materials table: iron burns when finely shaved, flint is harder than iron
ideas.idea: Each strike shaves iron particles whose size follows the strike energy; each particle flies ballistic with drag, heats by its own oxidation (Fe -> FeO heat release vs area) and cools by radiation and convection, glowing by its temperature (blackbody emission per particle in Hikari). A particle landing on tinder adds heat; tinder ignites above its temperature, smoulders, and Lumi's blow (air flow) grows it into flame. Someone watching sees orange sparks streak and die in the dusk, and one land.
ideas.form: plugin at the cliff: hold a key to strike; a dusk traced film, sparks as emissive points lighting Lumi's face

ideas.title: The tongue test
ideas.goal: The player builds a cell from what they find (a copper bead and an iron spike in a shell of brine) and checks it like a child with a battery: Lumi licks the two wires. Stack more cells and the zap gets stronger: Lumi's crest stands up, its face scrunches, the friends dare each other to try. Fun because it is a real, funny meter for current everyone understands.
ideas.toward: Road step 'two metals in brine make a cell': the first circuit, from what touches what
ideas.idea: Each cell's voltage comes from the two metals' electrode potentials in the materials table, its internal resistance from wetted area and spacing; cells in series add. The tongue is a resistor (~10 kOhm wet); the current through it sets how big the reaction is (face, crest, a jump). Wrong metals the same: nothing. Someone watching sees Lumi lick a row of shells and its crest bristle.
ideas.form: plugin + a circuit solver (nodal analysis over the contacts); a close traced film of the lick and the friends' faces

ideas.title: What is it made of? The beach test
ideas.goal: The player picks up anything on the island and tests it like a scientist with no lab: hold it to the magnet stone, drop it in brine, put it in the fire, lick it with a cell. Each test answers by the thing's real material, and finds sort into piles. Fun because the island turns into a puzzle box of materials, and some surprise you (the anchor chain is iron, the bell is bronze and ignores the stone).
ideas.toward: Road step 'one materials table read by every system', the backbone everything else reads
ideas.idea: world/materials.toml: density, conductivity, permeability, melting point, burns or not, for copper, iron, magnet stone, wood, brine, glass, bronze, stone. Every prop gets a material; em.jl, the kiln, buoyancy and the circuit read it. Someone watching sees Lumi try a seashell, a nail and a spoon on the stone; only one jumps.
ideas.form: engine table + a plugin for the tests; a film of three tests side by side

ideas.title: The bellows and the green rock
ideas.goal: The player pumps the kiln's bellows in a rhythm: too slow and the fire sulks, too fast and it burns the charcoal away; held right, green rock with charcoal gives tiny copper beads you pick out of the slag. Fun because the rhythm is learnable and the reward is the island's first metal.
ideas.toward: Road step 'copper from green rock: smelted in the kiln'
ideas.idea: A lumped kiln: air flow from the bellows' stroke, charcoal burning by oxygen supply, heat into the charge and out through the walls; malachite reduces to copper above ~1100 C with CO present (Ellingham), beads grow while it stays hot. Someone watching sees the kiln mouth go from red to yellow-white with each pump and Lumi lean on the bellows.
ideas.form: extend plugins kiln: bellows key, heat model, beads as props; a traced film of the glow

ideas.title: The draw plate
ideas.goal: The player pulls a copper rod through ever smaller holes in a stone plate; each pass is harder as the copper work-hardens, and it snaps if forced; heat it red in the fire and it pulls soft again. Fun because you feel the metal change and have to read when to anneal.
ideas.toward: Road step 'drawn into wire that keeps its bends' and the copper-wire project
ideas.idea: Wire drawing force from the reduction and the current yield stress (Hollomon hardening, recovered by annealing above ~400 C); the rod's length grows as its area shrinks, its diameter feeds physics/wire.jl so the result bends like wire of that size. Someone watching sees Lumi brace and pull, the wire lengthen, then glow in the fire.
ideas.form: plugin by the wire bench; a short film of three passes and a snap

ideas.title: The scrap crane
ideas.goal: The player winds a coil by turning a spindle with the beak, clips it to a cell row on a pole, swings it over the iron in the bay and switches it on and off: spikes, the anchor, a pot fly up and drop where you let go, on a friend's head if you are mean. Fun because how many turns and cells you used decides what it can lift.
ideas.toward: Road step 'a coil wound by turning a spindle lifts nails': the first electromagnet
ideas.idea: The coil is real geometry (turns along a helix), its field Biot-Savart from em.jl, its current from the cell circuit; lifted things are softiron bodies; the pole is a jointed lever. Someone watching sees a fistful of spikes leap to a coil and rain down when the switch opens.
ideas.form: plugin + a winding interaction; a film with a friend under the falling spikes

ideas.title: Where lightning goes
ideas.goal: In a storm the player raises a copper wire on a pole by the cottage and watches where the bolts land: the tallest, best-connected conductor takes them, the cottage is spared, and a poorly grounded rod scorches the grass. Fun because the storm becomes something you build against.
ideas.toward: The field solver deciding everything, at island scale: conductors, ground, materials
ideas.idea: A coarse 3D Laplace solve of the potential between cloud and island (conductors fixed at ground potential by their material and contact), then a dielectric-breakdown leader grown step by step toward the strongest field; where it lands is decided by what the player built. Someone watching sees a branching bolt pick the rod.
ideas.form: plugin into the storm; a night traced film with the bolt's light

ideas.title: A speaker made of paper and a coil
ideas.goal: The player glues a paper cone onto a little coil, sits it over the magnet stone, and wires it to the synth: out comes Lumi's tune, thin and buzzy or fuller by how many turns and how big the cone. Fun because you hear what you built.
ideas.toward: Coil, stone and fields doing work, and sound: the force on a current in the stone's field moves a part
ideas.idea: The coil current follows the synth signal; force = B*l*i on the coil in the stone's real field; the cone is a mass-spring-damper whose velocity times area is the sound pressure; played through the game audio. Someone watching sees the cone shiver and hears the island's first loudspeaker.
ideas.form: plugin with audio output; a film with sound
